The Silero voice-detection model is part of the `silero-vad` package.\n\n## Audio setup (Windows)\n\nNo virtual audio driver is needed. Windows can record \"what the speakers play\" through **WASAPI loopback**; the\nprogram records that loopback device for the call side and your microphone for `Me` — at the same time.\n\n1. **Plug in wired headphones first**, then start the program (device numbers are read at start-up).\n2. In the call app (Google Meet, Zoom, …) leave the **speaker/output on the Windows default device**, the one whose\n   loopback you record. You hear the call normally.\n3. Keep the **call volume moderate**. At normal volume our echo check found no call audio leaking into the headset\n   microphone; with a loud video it did, and those phrases were then labelled `Me` (echo handling is out of scope).\n4. List the devices:\n\n```powershell\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m hylive --list-devices\n```\n```\n   9  INPUT     2 ch  48000 Hz  Микрофон (Realtek(R) Audio)\n  10  LOOPBACK  2 ch  48000 Hz  Динамики (Realtek(R) Audio) [Loopback]\n```\n\nWithout flags the program uses the **Windows default microphone** and the **loopback of the default speakers**, and\nprints which ones it chose. Choose others with `--mic <INPUT index>` and `--system <LOOPBACK index>`.\n\nWhile capturing the call side, the program plays **digital silence** (inaudible) on those speakers: Windows sends no\nloopback data at all while nothing plays, which would stop phrase detection ([D-010, D-019](DECISIONS.md)).\n\n## Running\n\n```powershell\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m hylive                       # default devices\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m hylive --mic 9 --system 10   # chosen devices\n```\n\nWait for `Ready.` (all models are loaded and warmed up first), then talk / start the call. Stop with **Ctrl+C**: the\nprogram finishes the phrases it already heard and prints a summary per source:\n\n```\nmic    phrases detected: 4 (of which 1 at shutdown), printed: 4 (of which 0 discarded as repetitive), PortAudio problem flags: 0\n       latency: median 3.0 s, max 3.9 s, <= 5 s: 4/4 (100 %)\nsystem phrases detected: 16 (of which 0 at shutdown), printed: 16 (of which 0 discarded as repetitive), PortAudio problem flags: 0\n       latency: median 4.1 s, max 5.9 s, <= 5 s: 14/16 (88 %)\nspeakers identified on the system side: 2 (threshold 0.35)\n```\n\nEach block shows time (session clock, the same for both sides), speaker, Armenian, English, and a measurement line:\n`latency` = end of the spoken phrase → English line printed (the brief's definition), split into ASR, translation and\nspeaker time; `queue A+B` = phrases waiting for transcription + translation.\n\n| Option | Default | Meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| `--list-devices` | | print recordable devices and exit |\n| `--mic N`, `--system N` | Windows defaults | microphone / loopback device |\n| `--asr-model` | `large-v3` | faster-whisper model name |\n| `--max-segment-s` | `5` | longest phrase before it is cut (longer phrases broke the 5 s latency) |\n| `--min-silence-ms` | `500` | pause that ends a phrase |\n| `--speaker-threshold` | `0.35` | voice similarity needed to count as a known speaker |\n| `--sources` | `mic,system` | testing aid: `mic` or `system` only |\n\nSpecial lines you may see: `HY: (repetitive output discarded - likely noise or echo …)` — Whisper produced a\nrepetition loop (typical for noise, music or laughter); it is shown but not translated, and the speaker is shown as\n`Speaker ?`. `(cut at token limit)` — the output reached the safety limit of 128 tokens.\n\n## How it works\n\n```\n microphone ──► capture ──► 16 kHz mono ──► VAD + segmenter ──┐\n                                                              ├─► phrase queue ─► ASR thread (GPU) ─► text queue ─► translation thread (CPU) ─► terminal\n loopback ────► capture ──► 16 kHz mono ──► VAD + segmenter ──┘     Whisper large-v3            speaker label (system side) + NLLB\n (+ silent keep-alive on the speakers)\n```\n\n| Module | Input → output |\n|---|---|\n| `hylive/audio_capture.py` | device → 10 ms audio blocks (PortAudio callback, native 48 kHz stereo); device lookup; keep-alive silence |\n| `hylive/audio_convert.py` | blocks → 16 kHz mono float32 (channel average + streaming `soxr` resampler, no clicks at block edges) |\n| `hylive/segmenter.py` | 16 kHz audio → phrases (Silero VAD: phrase ends after 500 ms of silence; cut at 5 s; one VAD model per source) |\n| `hylive/asr.py` | phrase → Armenian text + reliability info (Whisper large-v3, beam 1, temperature 0, 128-token limit, repetition checks) |\n| `hylive/speakers.py` | phrase → `Speaker N` (voice fingerprint + online clustering) |\n| `hylive/translate.py` | Armenian → English (NLLB-200 600M via CTranslate2) |\n| `hylive/__main__.py` | command line, threads, output, summary, offline mode |\n\nDesign points:\n- **Two sources, one GPU.** Each source has its own capture and segmentation thread; one shared ASR thread uses the\n  GPU (one phrase at a time); a separate translation thread on the CPU lets the GPU start the next phrase while the\n  previous one is translated ([D-017, D-021](DECISIONS.md)).\n- **Bounded work per phrase.** Without limits, a Whisper repetition loop once took 7–8 s plus a 17–20 s translation\n  and the queue grew to 90 s of delay. Phrases are now cut at 5 s, Whisper output is limited, loops are detected and\n  discarded visibly, and translation length is limited ([D-020, D-025](DECISIONS.md)).\n- **Speaker identification.** For each call-side phrase, SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN computes a 192-number voice\n  fingerprint on the CPU. It is compared (cosine similarity) with each known speaker's average fingerprint: ≥ 0.35 →\n  that speaker, otherwise a new `Speaker N`. Phrases under 1 s never create a speaker. Everything from the microphone\n  is `Me` ([D-023](DECISIONS.md)).\n- **Fail loudly.** No silent fallbacks: wrong devices, missing models or a crashed thread stop the program with a\n  clear error; the summary shows detected vs. printed phrases so lost phrases would be visible.\n\n## Models: what was chosen and why\n\nAll decisions with the full reasoning and numbers are in [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md); measurements in [TESTS.md](TESTS.md).\n\n| Task | Chosen | Alternatives tested / considered | Why |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Speech recognition | **Whisper large-v3** via faster-whisper 1.2.1 (CTranslate2 4.8.3), GPU, `int8_float32`, beam 1 | small (CER 43 %), medium (37 %) on one test sentence; **large-v3-turbo**: 1.8× faster but CER 23.0 % vs 8.6 % on the 10-sentence set; beam 5: CER 6.4 % but max 3.7 s per phrase; Armenian initial prompt: CER 12.8 % (caused a hallucination) | Best Armenian accuracy that fits in 3 GB VRAM and stays fast enough (avg 1.7 s, max 1.9 s per phrase) |\n| GPU engine | CTranslate2 (in faster-whisper) | PyTorch on GPU | Current PyTorch CUDA builds dropped GTX 10-series (Pascal) support; CTranslate2 supports `int8` on this GPU. PyTorch is used on the CPU only |\n| Translation | **NLLB-200 distilled 600M**, converted to CTranslate2 int8, CPU | Helsinki-NLP opus-mt-hy-en (considered, not tested) | Explicit Armenian support; 0.3–0.9 s per phrase on the CPU, GPU stays free; 10/10 test sentences translated understandably. Rule set in advance: test opus-mt only if > 3/10 failed |\n| Voice detection | **Silero VAD** 6.2.3 (`VADIterator`) + own segmenter | Silero copy inside faster-whisper (internal, whole-file API); webrtcvad | Official streaming API; ~3 % of real time; also stops Whisper from transcribing silence |\n| Speaker identification | **SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN** (`speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb`), CPU | plain audio statistics; Whisper encoder output; ONNX speaker model (needs hand-written preprocessing) | Standard pretrained speaker model with built-in preprocessing, very little own code. Accepted only after a `pip --dry-run` showed it keeps our PyTorch and adds no large packages |\n| Resampling | soxr 1.1.0 (streaming) | PyAV, numpy decimation, scipy | Streaming filter state between 10 ms blocks; tiny dependency |\n| Audio capture | PyAudioWPatch 0.2.12.9 (WASAPI loopback) | soundcard; VB-Cable virtual driver | Loopback devices appear as normal inputs; no extra driver |\n\nLicences to be aware of: Whisper weights — MIT; Silero VAD — MIT; SpeechBrain — Apache 2.0 (see the model card of\n`spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb`); **NLLB-200 — CC-BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial use only)**.\n\n## Test results\n\nAll numbers come from runs on the target laptop; see [TESTS.md](TESTS.md) for every run, the method and the raw values.\n\n### Armenian transcription\nEvaluation set: 10 Armenian sentences read by me (laptop microphone), correct text in `eval/sentences.txt`, scored with\n`scripts/eval_asr.py` through the same path as the live program (CER = character error rate after removing punctuation).\n\n| Setting (large-v3) | CER | ASR time avg / max |\n|---|---|---|\n| **beam 1 (chosen)** | **8.6 %** | 1.67 s / 1.89 s |\n| beam 5 | 6.4 % | 2.80 s / 3.73 s |\n| beam 5 + Armenian prompt | 12.8 % | 2.50 s / 3.85 s |\n| beam 1, 300 ms padding | 7.7 % | 1.67 s / 1.87 s |\n| large-v3-turbo | 23.0 % | 0.93 s / 0.98 s |\n\n- Live through system audio (sentences played as the \"call side\"): CER **5.7 %**, identical to offline on the same clips.\n- Live, my own sentences over a playing video (headset mic): CER **12.4 %**.\n\n### English translation\n- From the correct Armenian text: **10/10** sentences understandable.\n- From Whisper's text (what the program shows): **2 correct, 3 gist, 5 wrong** — e.g. «սուրջ» instead of «սուրճ»\n  turned *coffee* into *seriously*. The translator is fine; transcription errors are the problem.\n\n### Speaker identification\nThree 60–80 s interview recordings with known speaker changes (`scripts/speaker_test.py`):\n\n| Recording | Wrong labels at threshold 0.35 | Same speaker similarity | New speaker's first phrase |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| man + woman | 0 | 0.54–0.77 | 0.21 |\n| same gender (first) | 0 (speaker returning after 20 s gets the same label) | 0.73–0.80 | 0.14 |\n| two women (laughing, overlap) | 0 | 0.51–0.88 | 0.16 |\n\nThresholds from 0.25 to 0.4/0.45 gave 0 errors on all three; 0.35 is in the middle. Live runs on the two-women clip\nand on the man + woman interview gave the correct speakers (2 of 2).\n\n### Latency (end of phrase → English line)\n\n| Run | Within 5 s | Median | Max |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Evaluation clips played as call side | 6/6 (100 %) | 2.8 s | 3.2 s |\n| Two-women interview, call side only, with speaker ID | 18/18 (100 %) | 3.9 s | 4.4 s |\n| Interview + speaker ID, user silent | 16/16 (100 %) | 4.0 s | 4.8 s |\n| Full program (interview + my speech): `Me` | 4/4 (100 %) | 3.0 s | 3.9 s |\n| Full program (interview + my speech): call side | 14/16 (88 %) | 4.1 s | 5.9 s |\n| Earlier run with overlapping speech + echo (before speaker ID) | 64–70 % | 4.1–4.8 s | 8.7 s |\n\nPhrases over 5 s came from: the first phrase after start-up, a repetition loop that a filter missed (since fixed), and\noverlapping speech on both sides (one GPU transcribes one phrase at a time).\n\n### Other checks\n- Both sources captured at the same time with 0 lost audio blocks (PortAudio problem flags 0 in all runs).\n- No phrase lost on Ctrl+C: detected = printed in every run (a shutdown bug that lost phrases was found and fixed).\n- **Offline**: full program with Wi-Fi off — all models load, no network access ([D-024](DECISIONS.md)).\n\n## Known limitations\n\n- **Armenian accuracy.** Word-initial «Բ» is often heard as «Վ» or dropped («Վարև» for «Բարև») in every setting\n  tested; one wrong letter can change the English meaning. Clear speech helps a lot (CER 8.6 % read vs ~21 % on a\n  spontaneous test recording).\n- **Mixed languages.** Russian and English words inside Armenian (out of scope in the brief) are written in Armenian\n  letters; translation recovers some (\"meeting\", \"Okay\") but not others («Давай» → \"the lady of liberty\").\n- **Latency under overlapping speech.** One GPU transcribes one phrase at a time (~1.5–3 s each). When both sides\n  talk at once, phrases wait and some exceed 5 s. The first phrase after start-up is also slower.\n- **Phrase cutting.** Phrases are cut at 5 s to keep latency down; long sentences are split, which makes some\n  translations choppy. If the speaker changes inside a phrase, its first 1–2 s get the previous speaker's label.\n- **Speaker identification** was tested on 60–80 s clips with 2 speakers, not yet on 10+ minute calls, more than\n  two people or real call compression (Meet/Zoom). Very short phrases keep the closest known speaker.\n- **Echo.** If the call is loud enough to leak from the headphones into the microphone, it is transcribed again as\n  `Me` (echo handling is out of scope). Use headphones and a moderate volume.\n- **Repetition filter.** A real phrase that repeats the same words many times could be discarded as a loop.\n- **Platform.** Windows only (WASAPI loopback) and an NVIDIA GPU is required; tested on one laptop.\n- **NLLB licence** is non-commercial.\n\n## What I would improve with more time\n\n1. **Better Armenian recognition:** evaluate community Whisper models fine-tuned on Armenian (converted to\n   CTranslate2) on the same evaluation set; collect a larger, more varied evaluation set (more speakers, real calls).\n2. **Throughput under overlap:** transcribe several waiting phrases in one GPU batch (faster-whisper has a batched\n   mode), or use a GPU with more memory/speed.\n3. **Smarter phrase cutting:** cut at short pauses near the 5 s limit instead of exactly at 5 s; detect speaker\n   changes inside a phrase.\n4. **Robustness:** longer sessions and real calls with several people; tune the speaker threshold on call audio;\n   simple echo suppression for setups without headphones.\n5. **Usability:** pick devices by name, handle headphones being plugged in during a session.\n\n## Repository layout\n\n```\nhylive/                 the program (python -m hylive)\nscripts/                tools used to build and test it:\n  gpu_smoke_test.py       GPU check            list_devices.py, record_test.py   devices / recordings\n  download_models.py      one-time downloads   convert_test.py, vad_test.py       resampling / VAD checks\n  asr_test.py, mt_test.py ASR / MT checks      record_eval.py, eval_asr.py        evaluation set + CER\n  play_eval.py            play clips as call   speaker_test.py                    speaker ID thresholds\neval/sentences.txt      evaluation sentences (audio is not committed)\nPLAN.md                 original plan         DECISIONS.md   every decision with reasons and numbers\nTESTS.md                all test results      TIMELOG.md     time spent (~20 h budget)\nHANDOVER.md             current state / next steps (used between work sessions)\nCLAUDE.md               project rules given to the AI assistant\nchats/                  complete, unedited AI chat transcripts (required by the brief)\nrequirements.txt        pinned package versions\n```\n\nNot committed (`.gitignore`): model weights (`models/`), audio recordings (`recordings/`, `eval/audio/`), the\nvirtual environment, secrets.\n\n## How this was built\n\nI worked with Claude Cowork as the only AI assistant, step by step: plan first, a thin end-to-end version early,\nthen improving the weakest part, deciding by measurements with rules set before each test. Every decision and test is\nwritten down in `DECISIONS.md` and `TESTS.md`; the complete conversations are in `chats/`.\nEOF\nwc -l README.md",
  "timeout_ms": 30000
}

## What we already know: mostly Whisper, not NLLB

| Test (10 evaluation sentences) | English understandable |
|---|---|
| NLLB on **your correct Armenian text** | **10/10** |
| NLLB on **Whisper's text** (what the app shows) | **2 correct, 3 gist, 5 wrong** |

With perfect input, NLLB works. **The losses come from Whisper's spelling errors**: «սուրջ» for «սուրճ» turned *coffee* into *seriously*, and «Վաժիշկը» turned *doctor* into *singer*. **But NLLB plays a part too:** a more robust translator might guess the meaning *despite* a misspelled word. So both sides are worth one test each.

## Plan for tomorrow (capped at about 2.5 h)

We have about 8 h left in total, and still need about 4 h for the real call, the fresh install and the rehearsal. So this block gets **at most 2.5 h**.

**Step 0: a measurable baseline (15 min).**
- I write **English reference translations** for the 10 sentences (`eval/translations.txt`), and you check them.
- `eval_asr.py --translate` also computes **chrF**, a standard automatic translation score based on character overlap with the reference (0–100). It's about 20 lines of code with no new dependency. Together with your correct/gist/wrong judgement, that gives **two numbers per setting**.

**Step 1: Whisper translates directly from the audio (20 min, no new model).**
- Whisper can also output **English straight from speech** (`task="translate"`). That skips the misspelled Armenian text, so it may be more robust. The open questions are its quality for Armenian and its time cost. We'd still need the Armenian line, so it may mean two GPU passes.

**Step 2: a larger NLLB (30 min).**
- **NLLB-200 distilled 1.3B** instead of 600M, on the **same Whisper text**. It's a one-time download (about 5 GB) and conversion to int8. The question is whether it handles misspellings better, and whether CPU time stays at about 1.5 s or less.

**Step 3: an Armenian-fine-tuned Whisper (45 min).**
- Community models trained further on Armenian speech exist on Hugging Face, but **I'll verify that a specific one exists, its reported results, its size, and that it converts to CTranslate2**, before downloading anything. It must fit in 3 GB of VRAM. We'd test **at most one**.

**Not considered (too big for your hardware):** SeamlessM4T and other speech-translation models with billions of parameters. They don't fit in 3 GB of VRAM, and would be far too slow on the CPU.

**The decision rule, set now:**
- A change is kept only if it gives **clearly better English** (at least +2 sentences moved up a category, *or* a clearly higher chrF) **and** stays within the latency budget (ASR max ≤ about 2.5 s, translation max ≤ about 1.5 s).
- If **two** options help, we combine them only if the combination is measured as well.

- Push the README URL change (`git push`).
- Request the chat export, and send the email when ready.

**2. chrF in `eval_asr.py --translate`.** chrF measures how many character sequences the translation shares with the reference, from 0 to 100. Sanity check: identical text = **100**; "drink *seriously*" = 67; "The *singer* will be *alive*…" = 55; "Wow, what do you look like?" = 17. It's useful for comparing settings; your correct/gist/wrong judgement stays the main measure.

Per sentence, it now prints the **English reference**, the **EN from correct Armenian** (NLLB's best case) and the **EN from ASR** (what the app shows), each with its chrF. At the end comes a **TRANSLATION** line with both chrF totals and the translation time.

**3. `--set` for `record_eval.py` and `eval_asr.py`.** `--set natural` uses `eval/sentences_natural.txt`, `eval/translations_natural.txt` and `eval/audio/natural/` (audio ignored by Git). Without the flag, everything works as before.

Two promising candidates turned up. Here's what I could verify, and my recommendation.

## Candidates for an Armenian fine-tuned Whisper (step 3)

| | **Chillarmo/whisper-large-v3-turbo-armenian** | BuzzASR/armenian |
|---|---|---|
| Base | Whisper large-v3-**turbo**, fine-tuned | Whisper large-v3, fully fine-tuned |
| Trained on | Common Voice 20 (Armenian) | FLEURS + Common Voice 25, plus Armenian text |
| Reported results (by the authors) | **CER 2.86%**, WER 15.3% (Common Voice held-out test) | **CER 3.72% FLEURS**, 0.65% Common Voice; claims 15.5% → 2.3% vs plain large-v3 |
| Licence | Apache-2.0 | MIT |
| Size / speed for us | 0.8B, **like turbo: about 0.9 s per phrase** (about half of large-v3!) | like large-v3 (about 1.8 s) |
| Works with our CTranslate2 engine? | **Very likely.** It's a normal fine-tune with the standard Whisper tokenizer; the converter recipe is documented by faster-whisper | **Risky.** Its card says it uses a "**native per-language tokenizer replacement**" with a "baked-in" prompt. faster-whisper relies on Whisper's standard tokens, so it may not work, and we can't run it on the GPU any other way (PyTorch GPU doesn't support your card) |

**One important caution:** these numbers are **self-reported, on read speech**, and with different test sets than ours. Plain turbo gave us 23% CER, but a *fine-tuned* turbo is a different model. **Only our own measurement counts.**

**Recommendation: test Chillarmo turbo-armenian first (and probably only that one).**
- It's the one most likely to *work* in our pipeline, it's documented, and it could **improve accuracy *and* halve ASR time**. The time saved would also be welcome for latency under overlapping speech.
- **BuzzASR stays a documented alternative**: "promising numbers, but its custom tokenizer is likely incompatible with CTranslate2 / faster-whisper on a Pascal GPU". That's an honest note for the README.

**Reordering the plan:** I'd do **step 3 before step 2** (the larger NLLB). Step 0 showed that **Whisper's errors cost about 19 chrF points**, so better ASR is the bigger lever. For step 2 there's a ready-made **CTranslate2 int8 conversion of NLLB-1.3B** ([winstxnhdw/nllb-200-distilled-1.3B-ct2-int8](https://huggingface.co/winstxnhdw/nllb-200-distilled-1.3B-ct2-int8)), which avoids a RAM-heavy conversion on your 8 GB laptop.

## Step 3: conversion (needs your OK; about 1.6–3 GB download, once)

This is the conversion recipe from the faster-whisper documentation, with the download kept on D:

```powershell
$env:HF_HOME = "D:\Em\mathrix\models\hf_home"
.\.venv\Scripts\ct2-transformers-converter.exe --model Chillarmo/whisper-large-v3-turbo-armenian --output_dir models\whisper-turbo-armenian-ct2 --copy_files tokenizer.json preprocessor_config.json --quantization int8
```

If it fails (for example, `tokenizer.json` missing from the repo), paste the error, and we stop or adjust it. **Then the evaluation**, same set and same settings, only the model changes:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\eval_asr.py --model models\whisper-turbo-armenian-ct2 --translate
```

**Decision rule (set now):** we switch the live default only if **CER is clearly lower than 8.6%** (≥ 2 points better) **and** the English improves (≥ +2 sentences up a category, or clearly higher chrF), with ASR time no worse than large-v3.

**Meanwhile:** your 6 natural sentences. As soon as you send them, I'll create the files. The new model must then also be tested on *natural* speech, not just read sentences.

**Time:** 14:20. Today's translation block has used about 40 minutes of its 2.5 h.

## Decision rule (set now)

**Baseline:** CER 8.6%, chrF 49.3, judgement 2 / 3 / 5, ASR max 2.08 s, MT max 0.53 s.

A setting is adopted only if:
- the English is **clearly better**: **≥ +2 sentences move up a category, or chrF +3 or more**;
- **and it keeps the latency budget**: **ASR max ≤ 2.6 s** and **MT max ≤ 0.8 s**, which keeps about 4.2 s per phrase plus margin for queuing;
- **and it doesn't get worse on the natural set.**

Otherwise we keep the current settings and document the results. Paste the outputs as they come.

| Setting | Tested? | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Whisper beam 5 | ✅ | CER 8.6% → **6.4%**, but max 3.7 s per phrase, too slow |

| **NLLB beam 4** (we use 2) | ❌ | the translator considers more alternatives; costs a little CPU time, no GPU time |

Our latency margin is about 1–1.5 s per phrase (ASR max about 2.1 s + speaker 0.5 + translation 0.5 + VAD 0.5 ≈ 3.6 s). That's why **beam 2 and 3** are worth measuring: they might fit where beam 5 didn't.

## `--anti-repeat`: clearly worse ❌

| | Baseline | Anti-repeat |
|---|---|---|
| CER | 8.6% | **17.9%** |
| chrF | 49.3 | **36.6** |
| ASR max | 2.08 s | 2.13 s |

**The likely cause, which is useful for the README:** Whisper writes Armenian with **byte-level tokens**. Each Armenian letter takes 2 bytes, and the same small token pieces naturally repeat many times inside normal Armenian words. **`no_repeat_ngram_size=3` forbids repeating any 3-token sequence**, so it blocks *legitimate* Armenian spellings and forces wrong letters:
- «վերադար**ց**ել» instead of «վերադարձել»;
- «շնորհակա**ր**ություն» instead of «շնորհակալություն»;
- and in sentence 10, Whisper simply **stopped early**: «ես սիրում են։», giving "I like it."

Only sentence 07 improved ("It was raining last night." ✅). It's not worth the losses. **Rejected; no step 2 needed for it.**

It wins on **all three sets**. **Decision: turbo-armenian becomes the default**, and large-v3 stays available as a fallback (`--asr-model large-v3`).

## Quick look at c03, c04 and c05

| # | Problem | Quick fix? |
|---|---|---|
| **c03** | Whisper wrote «**- Չեմ հասկանում… - Կարո՞՞ւ ես…**». Both halves are recognised almost correctly, but the **dialog dashes "- " and the "…"** made NLLB treat it as a dialogue and **drop the first sentence** | ✅ **Yes, and it's general.** The turbo model has a style habit of starting with "- " and ending with "…". Cleaning that punctuation before translation is a fix for *all* outputs, not this sentence |
| c04 | «կա**տ**» for «կա**թ**» (թ/տ sound almost the same) → "goats" | ❌ acoustic, no general fix |
| c05 | «Երե**ք**» for «Երե**կ**», and the end «դուր չեկավ» is **missing**. Probably the 8-second recording ended before you finished this long sentence | ❌ acoustic, plus likely the recording length |

**I'm adding the punctuation cleanup now.** It's one small function in `asr.py`: remove dialog dashes at the start of a sentence ("- " with a space; real hyphens inside words are kept), turn "…" into ".", and collapse "՞՞" into "՞". It applies to both models.
```
This block is not supported on your current device yet.
```

The cleanup works as intended on real outputs. The dialog dashes and "…" are gone, while **hyphens inside words** («project-ը», «2-3») and normal text are untouched:

```
'- Չեմ հասկանում… - Կարո՞՞ւ ես…'  →  'Չեմ հասկանում. Կարո՞ւ ես մի քիչ դանդախ խոսել.'
'Մեր project-ը գրեթե պատրաստ է'   →  unchanged
```

## What has already been tried (so we don't repeat it)

| Area | Already tested | With which model |
|---|---|---|
| Model | small, medium, large-v3, plain turbo, **turbo-armenian ✅ (now the default)** | — |
| Whisper settings | beam 2/3/5, Armenian prompt, anti-repeat, task=translate | **only on large-v3** |
| Audio | loudness normalisation, 300 ms padding | large-v3 |
| Text | punctuation cleanup ✅ | turbo-armenian |
| VAD / chunking | 500 ms silence and 5 s maximum, **never varied** | — |

**The key point:** every setting experiment was done on large-v3, which was slow. **turbo-armenian takes about 1.0 s per phrase, so we now have time budget that we didn't have before.** That makes two untried ideas the most promising:

# hylive — live Armenian → English transcription in the terminal

A Python program that listens to a live conversation (your microphone **and** the other side of a call),
transcribes spoken Armenian, translates it to English and prints each phrase with time and speaker:

```
[00:00:39] Speaker 2
HY: Ներքին ճանապար էս անցել, որովհետև ներքին ինքն աբավությու
EN: I went through the inner path, because the inner self is the abomination.
    latency 4.0 s (ASR 2.5 s, translation 0.9 s, speaker 0.6 s, similarity 0.23, queue 0+0)

[00:00:23] Me
HY: խոսում են կին և տղամարդ։
EN: It's a woman and a man.
    latency 3.0 s (ASR 1.8 s, translation 0.7 s, queue 0+0)
```
(Real output from a test run; the spelling errors in the first block are Whisper's.)

Everything runs **locally** on the laptop (no cloud APIs); it was verified with Wi-Fi switched off.
Built for the Mathrix AI coding challenge on Windows 11 with an NVIDIA GTX 1060 (3 GB).

Honest summary of the result (details in [Test results](#test-results)):
- All required features work live: two audio sources at once, Armenian transcription, English translation,
  `Me` / `Speaker 1` / `Speaker 2` labels that stay stable, live terminal output.
- Latency: after the latency fixes, with one person speaking at a time, 93–100 % of phrases appeared within 5 s
  (median 2.8–4.0 s).
  **Not every phrase meets the 5 s target**: with overlapping speech the worst observed case was 8.7 s
  (64–70 % within 5 s), because one GPU transcribes one phrase at a time.
- Accuracy is the main limitation: Armenian is a low-resource language. Character error rate (CER) was 8.6 % on
  clearly read sentences, but small spelling errors often change the meaning of the English translation.

## Requirements

| | Tested with | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| OS | Windows 11 | System audio is captured with **WASAPI loopback** (Windows only) |
| GPU | NVIDIA GTX 1060 3 GB, driver 582.28 | Required: Whisper runs on the GPU with `int8_float32`. CUDA 12 libraries are installed by pip; no CUDA Toolkit needed |
| Python | 3.12 (`py -3.12`) | |
| RAM | 8 GB | Whisper on GPU; translation, voice detection and speaker model on CPU |
| Disk | ~7 GB for models | Keep the project on a drive with space; all models go into `models\` |
| Headphones | wired headphones | So the call audio does not leak into your microphone (see [Audio setup](#audio-setup-windows)) |

Do **not** update the NVIDIA driver on a GTX 10-series card without reason: NVIDIA's 580 driver branch is the last
one that supports this GPU generation ([D-005](DECISIONS.md)).

## Installation

All commands: a **normal (non-administrator) PowerShell**, in the project folder.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/EmmaHarutyunyan/live-speech-translation.git
cd live-speech-translation

# 1. Virtual environment (no activation needed; we always call its python.exe directly)
py -3.12 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install --upgrade pip
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
```

`requirements.txt` pins every package that was tested, including the NVIDIA cuBLAS/cuDNN libraries
(`nvidia-cublas-cu12`, `nvidia-cudnn-cu12`) and the CPU build of PyTorch.

```powershell
# 2. Check that the GPU works (downloads Whisper "tiny", ~75 MB)
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\gpu_smoke_test.py          # must end with "SUCCESS"

# 3. Download the models into models\ (needs internet, once: Whisper large-v3 ~3 GB, NLLB tokenizer, speaker model)
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\download_models.py

# 4. Convert the NLLB translation model to CTranslate2 int8 (needs internet, once; downloads ~2.5 GB)
#    HF_HOME keeps the download inside the project instead of C:\Users\<you>\.cache
$env:HF_HOME = "$PWD\models\hf_home"
.\.venv\Scripts\ct2-transformers-converter.exe --model facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M `
    --output_dir models\nllb-200-distilled-600M-ct2-int8 --quantization int8
```

After these steps the program runs **without internet**: it sets `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` itself and loads every model
from `models\` ([D-024](DECISIONS.md)). The Silero voice-detection model is part of the `silero-vad` package.

## Audio setup (Windows)

No virtual audio driver is needed. Windows can record "what the speakers play" through **WASAPI loopback**; the
program records that loopback device for the call side and your microphone for `Me` — at the same time.

1. **Plug in wired headphones first**, then start the program (device numbers are read at start-up).
2. In the call app (Google Meet, Zoom, …) leave the **speaker/output on the Windows default device**, the one whose
   loopback you record. You hear the call normally.
3. Keep the **call volume moderate**. At normal volume our echo check found no call audio leaking into the headset
   microphone; with a loud video it did, and those phrases were then labelled `Me` (echo handling is out of scope).
4. List the devices:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m hylive --list-devices
```
```
   9  INPUT     2 ch  48000 Hz  Микрофон (Realtek(R) Audio)
  10  LOOPBACK  2 ch  48000 Hz  Динамики (Realtek(R) Audio) [Loopback]
```

Without flags the program uses the **Windows default microphone** and the **loopback of the default speakers**, and
prints which ones it chose. Choose others with `--mic <INPUT index>` and `--system <LOOPBACK index>`.

While capturing the call side, the program plays **digital silence** (inaudible) on those speakers: Windows sends no
loopback data at all while nothing plays, which would stop phrase detection ([D-010, D-019](DECISIONS.md)).

## Running

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m hylive                       # default devices
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m hylive --mic 9 --system 10   # chosen devices
```

Wait for `Ready.` (all models are loaded and warmed up first), then talk / start the call. Stop with **Ctrl+C**: the
program finishes the phrases it already heard and prints a summary per source:

```
mic    phrases detected: 4 (of which 1 at shutdown), printed: 4 (of which 0 discarded as repetitive), PortAudio problem flags: 0
       latency: median 3.0 s, max 3.9 s, <= 5 s: 4/4 (100 %)
system phrases detected: 16 (of which 0 at shutdown), printed: 16 (of which 0 discarded as repetitive), PortAudio problem flags: 0
       latency: median 4.1 s, max 5.9 s, <= 5 s: 14/16 (88 %)
speakers identified on the system side: 2 (threshold 0.35)
```

Each block shows time (session clock, the same for both sides), speaker, Armenian, English, and a measurement line:
`latency` = end of the spoken phrase → English line printed (the brief's definition), split into ASR, translation and
speaker time; `queue A+B` = phrases waiting for transcription + translation.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--list-devices` | | print recordable devices and exit |
| `--mic N`, `--system N` | Windows defaults | microphone / loopback device |
| `--asr-model` | `large-v3` | faster-whisper model name |
| `--max-segment-s` | `5` | longest phrase before it is cut (longer phrases broke the 5 s latency) |
| `--min-silence-ms` | `500` | pause that ends a phrase |
| `--speaker-threshold` | `0.35` | voice similarity needed to count as a known speaker |
| `--sources` | `mic,system` | testing aid: `mic` or `system` only |

Special lines you may see: `HY: (repetitive output discarded - likely noise or echo …)` — Whisper produced a
repetition loop (typical for noise, music or laughter); it is shown but not translated, and the speaker is shown as
`Speaker ?`. `(cut at token limit)` — the output reached the safety limit of 128 tokens.

## How it works

```
 microphone ──► capture ──► 16 kHz mono ──► VAD + segmenter ──┐
                                                              ├─► phrase queue ─► ASR thread (GPU) ─► text queue ─► translation thread (CPU) ─► terminal
 loopback ────► capture ──► 16 kHz mono ──► VAD + segmenter ──┘     Whisper large-v3            speaker label (system side) + NLLB
 (+ silent keep-alive on the speakers)
```

| Module | Input → output |
|---|---|
| `hylive/audio_capture.py` | device → 10 ms audio blocks (PortAudio callback, native 48 kHz stereo); device lookup; keep-alive silence |
| `hylive/audio_convert.py` | blocks → 16 kHz mono float32 (channel average + streaming `soxr` resampler, no clicks at block edges) |
| `hylive/segmenter.py` | 16 kHz audio → phrases (Silero VAD: phrase ends after 500 ms of silence; cut at 5 s; one VAD model per source) |
| `hylive/asr.py` | phrase → Armenian text + reliability info (Whisper large-v3, beam 1, temperature 0, 128-token limit, repetition checks) |
| `hylive/speakers.py` | phrase → `Speaker N` (voice fingerprint + online clustering) |
| `hylive/translate.py` | Armenian → English (NLLB-200 600M via CTranslate2) |
| `hylive/__main__.py` | command line, threads, output, summary, offline mode |

Design points:
- **Two sources, one GPU.** Each source has its own capture and segmentation thread; one shared ASR thread uses the
  GPU (one phrase at a time); a separate translation thread on the CPU lets the GPU start the next phrase while the
  previous one is translated ([D-017, D-021](DECISIONS.md)).
- **Bounded work per phrase.** Without limits, a Whisper repetition loop once took 7–8 s plus a 17–20 s translation
  and the queue grew to 90 s of delay. Phrases are now cut at 5 s, Whisper output is limited, loops are detected and
  discarded visibly, and translation length is limited ([D-020, D-025](DECISIONS.md)).
- **Speaker identification.** For each call-side phrase, SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN computes a 192-number voice
  fingerprint on the CPU. It is compared (cosine similarity) with each known speaker's average fingerprint: ≥ 0.35 →
  that speaker, otherwise a new `Speaker N`. Phrases under 1 s never create a speaker. Everything from the microphone
  is `Me` ([D-023](DECISIONS.md)).
- **Fail loudly.** No silent fallbacks: wrong devices, missing models or a crashed thread stop the program with a
  clear error; the summary shows detected vs. printed phrases so lost phrases would be visible.

## Models: what was chosen and why

All decisions with the full reasoning and numbers are in [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md); measurements in [TESTS.md](TESTS.md).

| Task | Chosen | Alternatives tested / considered | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Speech recognition | **Whisper large-v3** via faster-whisper 1.2.1 (CTranslate2 4.8.3), GPU, `int8_float32`, beam 1 | small (CER 43 %), medium (37 %) on one test sentence; **large-v3-turbo**: 1.8× faster but CER 23.0 % vs 8.6 % on the 10-sentence set; beam 5: CER 6.4 % but max 3.7 s per phrase; Armenian initial prompt: CER 12.8 % (caused a hallucination) | Best Armenian accuracy that fits in 3 GB VRAM and stays fast enough (avg 1.7 s, max 1.9 s per phrase) |
| GPU engine | CTranslate2 (in faster-whisper) | PyTorch on GPU | Current PyTorch CUDA builds dropped GTX 10-series (Pascal) support; CTranslate2 supports `int8` on this GPU. PyTorch is used on the CPU only |
| Translation | **NLLB-200 distilled 600M**, converted to CTranslate2 int8, CPU | Helsinki-NLP opus-mt-hy-en (considered, not tested) | Explicit Armenian support; 0.3–0.9 s per phrase on the CPU, GPU stays free; 10/10 test sentences translated understandably. Rule set in advance: test opus-mt only if > 3/10 failed |
| Voice detection | **Silero VAD** 6.2.3 (`VADIterator`) + own segmenter | Silero copy inside faster-whisper (internal, whole-file API); webrtcvad | Official streaming API; ~3 % of real time; also stops Whisper from transcribing silence |
| Speaker identification | **SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN** (`speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb`), CPU | plain audio statistics; Whisper encoder output; ONNX speaker model (needs hand-written preprocessing) | Standard pretrained speaker model with built-in preprocessing, very little own code. Accepted only after a `pip --dry-run` showed it keeps our PyTorch and adds no large packages |
| Resampling | soxr 1.1.0 (streaming) | PyAV, numpy decimation, scipy | Streaming filter state between 10 ms blocks; tiny dependency |
| Audio capture | PyAudioWPatch 0.2.12.9 (WASAPI loopback) | soundcard; VB-Cable virtual driver | Loopback devices appear as normal inputs; no extra driver |

Licences to be aware of: Whisper weights — MIT; Silero VAD — MIT; SpeechBrain — Apache 2.0 (see the model card of
`spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb`); **NLLB-200 — CC-BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial use only)**.

## Test results

All numbers come from runs on the target laptop; see [TESTS.md](TESTS.md) for every run, the method and the raw values.

### Armenian transcription
Evaluation set: 10 Armenian sentences read by me (laptop microphone), correct text in `eval/sentences.txt`, scored with
`scripts/eval_asr.py` through the same path as the live program (CER = character error rate after removing punctuation).

| Setting (large-v3) | CER | ASR time avg / max |
|---|---|---|
| **beam 1 (chosen)** | **8.6 %** | 1.67 s / 1.89 s |
| beam 5 | 6.4 % | 2.80 s / 3.73 s |
| beam 5 + Armenian prompt | 12.8 % | 2.50 s / 3.85 s |
| beam 1, 300 ms padding | 7.7 % | 1.67 s / 1.87 s |
| large-v3-turbo | 23.0 % | 0.93 s / 0.98 s |

- Live through system audio (sentences played as the "call side"): CER **5.7 %**, identical to offline on the same clips.
- Live, my own sentences over a playing video (headset mic): CER **12.4 %**.

### English translation
- From the correct Armenian text: **10/10** sentences understandable.
- From Whisper's text (what the program shows): **2 correct, 3 gist, 5 wrong** — e.g. «սուրջ» instead of «սուրճ»
  turned *coffee* into *seriously*. The translator is fine; transcription errors are the problem.

### Speaker identification
Three 60–80 s interview recordings with known speaker changes (`scripts/speaker_test.py`):

| Recording | Wrong labels at threshold 0.35 | Same speaker similarity | New speaker's first phrase |
|---|---|---|---|
| man + woman | 0 | 0.54–0.77 | 0.21 |
| same gender (first) | 0 (speaker returning after 20 s gets the same label) | 0.73–0.80 | 0.14 |
| two women (laughing, overlap) | 0 | 0.51–0.88 | 0.16 |

Thresholds 0.35 and 0.4 gave 0 errors on all three recordings (0.25–0.3 were tested on two of them, 0.45–0.5 on
one, also with 0 errors; 0.2 merged two speakers, 0.55 created extra ones). 0.35 is in the middle of the safe range. Live runs on the two-women clip
and on the man + woman interview gave the correct speakers (2 of 2).

### Latency (end of phrase → English line)

| Run | Within 5 s | Median | Max |
|---|---|---|---|
| Evaluation clips played as call side | 6/6 (100 %) | 2.8 s | 3.2 s |
| Two-women interview, call side only, with speaker ID | 18/18 (100 %) | 3.9 s | 4.4 s |
| Interview + speaker ID, user silent | 16/16 (100 %) | 4.0 s | 4.8 s |
| Full program (interview + my speech): `Me` | 4/4 (100 %) | 3.0 s | 3.9 s |
| Full program (interview + my speech): call side | 14/16 (88 %) | 4.1 s | 5.9 s |
| Earlier run with overlapping speech + echo (before speaker ID) | 64–70 % | 4.1–4.8 s | 8.7 s |

Phrases over 5 s came from: the first phrase after start-up, a repetition loop that the filter missed (a stricter
rule was added afterwards and checked on the recorded text, not yet in a new live run), and overlapping speech on both
sides (one GPU transcribes one phrase at a time).

### Other checks
- Both sources captured at the same time with 0 lost audio blocks (PortAudio problem flags 0 in all runs).
- No phrase lost on Ctrl+C: detected = printed in every run (a shutdown bug that lost phrases was found and fixed).
- **Offline**: full program with Wi-Fi off — all models load, no network access ([D-024](DECISIONS.md)).

## Known limitations

- **Armenian accuracy.** Word-initial «Բ» is often heard as «Վ» or dropped («Վարև» for «Բարև») in every setting
  tested; one wrong letter can change the English meaning. Clear speech helps a lot (CER 8.6 % read vs ~21 % on a
  spontaneous test recording).
- **Mixed languages.** Russian and English words inside Armenian (out of scope in the brief) are written in Armenian
  letters; translation recovers some ("meeting", "Okay") but not others («Давай» → "the lady of liberty").
- **Latency under overlapping speech.** One GPU transcribes one phrase at a time (~1.5–3 s each). When both sides
  talk at once, phrases wait and some exceed 5 s. The first phrase after start-up is also slower.
- **Phrase cutting.** Phrases are cut at 5 s to keep latency down; long sentences are split, which makes some
  translations choppy. If the speaker changes inside a phrase, its first 1–2 s get the previous speaker's label.
- **Speaker identification** was tested on 60–80 s clips with 2 speakers, not yet on 10+ minute calls, more than
  two people or real call compression (Meet/Zoom). Very short phrases keep the closest known speaker.
- **Echo.** If the call is loud enough to leak from the headphones into the microphone, it is transcribed again as
  `Me` (echo handling is out of scope). Use headphones and a moderate volume.
- **Repetition filter.** A real phrase that repeats the same words many times could be discarded as a loop.
- **Platform.** Windows only (WASAPI loopback) and an NVIDIA GPU is required; tested on one laptop.
- **NLLB licence** is non-commercial.

## What I would improve with more time

1. **Better Armenian recognition:** evaluate community Whisper models fine-tuned on Armenian (converted to
   CTranslate2) on the same evaluation set; collect a larger, more varied evaluation set (more speakers, real calls).
2. **Throughput under overlap:** transcribe several waiting phrases in one GPU batch (faster-whisper has a batched
   mode), or use a GPU with more memory/speed.
3. **Smarter phrase cutting:** cut at short pauses near the 5 s limit instead of exactly at 5 s; detect speaker
   changes inside a phrase.
4. **Robustness:** longer sessions and real calls with several people; tune the speaker threshold on call audio;
   simple echo suppression for setups without headphones.
5. **Usability:** pick devices by name, handle headphones being plugged in during a session.

## Repository layout

```
hylive/                 the program (python -m hylive)
scripts/                tools used to build and test it:
  gpu_smoke_test.py       GPU check            list_devices.py, record_test.py   devices / recordings
  download_models.py      one-time downloads   convert_test.py, vad_test.py       resampling / VAD checks
  asr_test.py, mt_test.py ASR / MT checks      record_eval.py, eval_asr.py        evaluation set + CER
  play_eval.py            play clips as call   speaker_test.py                    speaker ID thresholds
eval/sentences.txt      evaluation sentences (audio is not committed)
PLAN.md                 original plan         DECISIONS.md   every decision with reasons and numbers
TESTS.md                all test results      TIMELOG.md     time spent (~20 h budget)
HANDOVER.md             current state / next steps (used between work sessions)
CLAUDE.md               project rules given to the AI assistant
chats/                  complete, unedited AI chat transcripts (required by the brief)
requirements.txt        pinned package versions
```

Not committed (`.gitignore`): model weights (`models/`), audio recordings (`recordings/`, `eval/audio/`), the
virtual environment, secrets.

I worked with Claude Cowork as the only AI assistant, step by step: plan first, a thin end-to-end version early,
then improving the weakest part, deciding by measurements with rules set before each test. Every decision and test is
written down in `DECISIONS.md` and `TESTS.md`; the complete conversations are in `chats/`.

## D-027 — Default ASR model: Armenian fine-tuned Whisper large-v3-turbo + punctuation cleanup (2026-10-29)
- **Decision:** `Chillarmo/whisper-large-v3-turbo-armenian` (Apache-2.0; fine-tuned on Common Voice Armenian),
  converted to CTranslate2 int8 into `models/whisper-turbo-armenian-ct2`, is the default (`--asr-model`).
  large-v3 stays available as a fallback (`download_models.py --with-large-v3`, `--asr-model large-v3`).
  New `clean_punctuation()` removes the model's subtitle-style dialog dashes, "…" and doubled "՞" before translation.
- **Why:** the only change that clearly improved accuracy (12 setting variations of large-v3 did not). Rule set in
  advance (CER ≥ 2 points better on read AND natural sets, English clearly better, ASR not slower) met on all three
  sets, incl. 5 sentences recorded fresh for this comparison (TESTS.md). ASR ~2× faster (≈1.0–1.5 s per phrase).
  It replaces large-v3, so the reviewer downloads less (~1.6 GB instead of ~3 GB); no new dependency.
- **Setup simplified:** `scripts/download_models.py` now downloads and converts both models itself
  (`ctranslate2.converters.TransformersConverter`), so setup = `pip install -r requirements.txt` + this one script.
- **Earlier decision revised:** D-026 (no new models) was the user's simplicity choice; reopened on 2026-10-29 because
  accuracy was the top concern and this model replaces rather than adds.
- **Status:** Verified 2026-10-29.

## D-028 — Whisper beam 5 with the turbo-armenian model (2026-10-31)
- **Decision:** live default `--asr-beam 5` (was 1). `--asr-beam 1` restores the old behaviour.
- **Why:** on large-v3, beam 5 was the only setting that lowered CER but was too slow (D-018). turbo-armenian is ~2×
  faster, so beam 5 now costs almost nothing (ASR max 1.89 s vs 1.80 s). Better or equal on all three test sets
  (read CER 1.9 → 1.3 %, natural 20.6 → 19.5 %, check unchanged; WER also lower).
- **Honest note:** the combined improvement (9.25 → 8.64 % CER) is below the 1-point threshold set before the test.
  Adopted anyway because no set got worse and there is no latency cost; recorded as an exception to the rule.
- **Rejected in the same run:** 800 ms end-of-phrase silence (no gain). Accuracy work stopped here (time limit).
- **Status:** Verified 2026-10-31 (live mic: 8/8 ≤ 5 s, median 2.1 s).

"""Download and prepare all models in models/ once, during setup (needs internet). Afterwards the program
runs offline (D-024). This is the only setup step after installing requirements.txt.

Run from the project folder:
    .\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe scripts\\download_models.py
    .\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe scripts\\download_models.py --with-large-v3   (also the fallback ASR model, ~3 GB)
"""

import os
from pathlib import Path

PROJECT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
os.environ["HF_HUB_OFFLINE"] = "0"  # this script is the one place that is allowed to download
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HOME", str(PROJECT_DIR / "models" / "hf_home"))  # keep downloads inside the project (D-004)

import argparse  # noqa: E402
import sys  # noqa: E402

sys.path.insert(0, str(PROJECT_DIR))

from hylive.asr import DEFAULT_MODEL_DIR, MODELS_DIR, Transcriber  # noqa: E402  (imported first: NVIDIA DLLs)
import transformers  # noqa: E402
from ctranslate2.converters import TransformersConverter  # noqa: E402

from hylive.speakers import SpeakerEncoder  # noqa: E402
from hylive.translate import MODEL_DIR as NLLB_DIR, SOURCE_LANG, TOKENIZER_NAME  # noqa: E402

ASR_SOURCE = "Chillarmo/whisper-large-v3-turbo-armenian"  # Armenian fine-tuned Whisper large-v3-turbo (D-027)
NLLB_SOURCE = "facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M"


def convert(source: str, output_dir: Path, copy_files: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    """Download a Hugging Face model and convert it to CTranslate2 int8 (skipped if already converted)."""
    if output_dir.exists():
        print(f"   already there: {output_dir.relative_to(PROJECT_DIR)}")
        return
    TransformersConverter(source, copy_files=copy_files).convert(str(output_dir), quantization="int8")
    print(f"   converted: {output_dir.relative_to(PROJECT_DIR)}")

`similarity` = voice match with the chosen speaker; `queue A+B` = phrases waiting for transcription +\ntranslation.\n\n| Option | Default | Meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| `--list-devices` | | print recordable devices and exit |\n| `--mic N`, `--system N` | Windows defaults | microphone / loopback device |\n| `--asr-model` | Armenian Whisper turbo in `models\\` | path or faster-whisper name (e.g. `large-v3` after `--with-large-v3`) |\n| `--asr-beam` | `5` | Whisper beam size |\n| `--max-segment-s` | `5` | longest phrase before it is cut (longer phrases broke the 5 s latency) |\n| `--min-silence-ms` | `500` | pause that ends a phrase |\n| `--speaker-threshold` | `0.35` | voice similarity needed to count as a known speaker |\n| `--sources` | `mic,system` | testing aid: `mic` or `system` only |\n\nSpecial lines you may see: `HY: (repetitive output discarded - likely noise or echo …)` means Whisper produced a\nrepetition loop (typical for noise, music or laughter); it is shown but not translated, and the speaker is shown as\n`Speaker ?`. `(cut at token limit)` means the output reached the safety limit of 128 tokens.\n\n## How it works\n\n```\n microphone ──► capture ──► 16 kHz mono ──► VAD + segmenter ──┐\n                                                              ├─► phrase queue ─► ASR thread (GPU) ─► text queue ─► translation thread (CPU) ─► terminal\n loopback ────► capture ──► 16 kHz mono ──► VAD + segmenter ──┘     Whisper (Armenian turbo)    speaker label (call side) + NLLB\n (+ silent keep-alive on the speakers)\n```\n\n| Module | Input → output |\n|---|---|\n| `hylive/audio_capture.py` | device → 10 ms audio blocks (PortAudio callback, native 48 kHz stereo); device lookup; keep-alive silence |\n| `hylive/audio_convert.py` | blocks → 16 kHz mono float32 (channel average + streaming `soxr` resampler, no clicks at block edges) |\n| `hylive/segmenter.py` | 16 kHz audio → phrases (Silero VAD: phrase ends after 500 ms of silence; cut at 5 s; one VAD model per source) |\n| `hylive/asr.py` | phrase → Armenian text + reliability info (beam 5, temperature 0, 128-token limit, repetition checks, punctuation cleanup) |\n| `hylive/speakers.py` | phrase → `Speaker N` (voice fingerprint + online clustering) |\n| `hylive/translate.py` | Armenian → English (NLLB-200 600M via CTranslate2) |\n| `hylive/__main__.py` | command line, threads, output, summary, offline mode |\n\nDesign points:\n- **Two sources, one GPU.** Each source has its own capture and segmentation thread; one shared ASR thread uses the\n  GPU (one phrase at a time); a separate translation thread on the CPU lets the GPU start the next phrase while the\n  previous one is translated ([D-017, D-021](DECISIONS.md)).\n- **Bounded work per phrase.** Without limits, a Whisper repetition loop once took 7–8 s plus a 17–20 s translation\n  and the queue grew to 90 s of delay. Phrases are now cut at 5 s, Whisper output is limited, loops are detected and\n  discarded visibly, and translation length is limited ([D-020, D-025](DECISIONS.md)).\n- **Speaker identification.** For each call-side phrase, SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN computes a 192-number voice\n  fingerprint on the CPU. It is compared (cosine similarity) with each known speaker's average fingerprint: ≥ 0.35 →\n  that speaker, otherwise a new `Speaker N`. Phrases under 1 s never create a speaker. Everything from the microphone\n  is `Me` ([D-023](DECISIONS.md)).\n- **Fail loudly.** No silent fallbacks: wrong devices, missing models or a crashed thread stop the program with a\n  clear error; the summary shows detected vs. printed phrases so lost phrases would be visible.\n\n## Models: what was chosen and why\n\nAll decisions with the full reasoning and numbers are in [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md); measurements in [TESTS.md](TESTS.md).\n\n| Task | Chosen | Alternatives tested / considered | Why |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Speech recognition | **`Chillarmo/whisper-large-v3-turbo-armenian`** (Whisper large-v3-turbo fine-tuned on Common Voice Armenian), converted to CTranslate2 int8, run with faster-whisper 1.2.1 on the GPU, beam 5 | Whisper small and medium (CER 43 % / 37 % on one test sentence); **large-v3** (previous default: CER 8.6 % read / 27.2 % natural, 12 setting variations tried without a clear gain); plain large-v3-turbo (CER 23 %) | Clearly the most accurate on all three test sets, and about twice as fast as large-v3 (≈1.0–1.5 s per phrase), so beam 5 costs almost no latency ([D-027, D-028](DECISIONS.md)) |\n| GPU engine | CTranslate2 (in faster-whisper) | PyTorch on GPU | Current PyTorch CUDA builds dropped GTX 10-series (Pascal) support; CTranslate2 supports `int8` on this GPU. PyTorch is used on the CPU only |\n| Translation | **NLLB-200 distilled 600M**, converted to CTranslate2 int8, CPU, beam 2 | Helsinki-NLP opus-mt-hy-en (considered); larger beams, Whisper's own speech translation (tested, not better) | Explicit Armenian support; 0.3–0.9 s per phrase on the CPU, GPU stays free; 10/10 correct Armenian test sentences translated understandably |\n| Voice detection | **Silero VAD** 6.2.3 (`VADIterator`) + own segmenter | Silero copy inside faster-whisper (internal, whole-file API); webrtcvad | Official streaming API; ~3 % of real time; also stops Whisper from transcribing silence |\n| Speaker identification | **SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN** (`speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb`), CPU | plain audio statistics; Whisper encoder output; ONNX speaker model (needs hand-written preprocessing) | Standard pretrained speaker model with built-in preprocessing, very little own code; keeps the existing PyTorch and adds no large packages |\n| Resampling | soxr 1.1.0 (streaming) | PyAV, numpy decimation, scipy | Streaming filter state between 10 ms blocks; tiny dependency |\n| Audio capture | PyAudioWPatch 0.2.12.9 (WASAPI loopback) | soundcard; VB-Cable virtual driver | Loopback devices appear as normal inputs; no extra driver |\n\nLicences: Armenian Whisper turbo — Apache 2.0; Whisper — MIT; Silero VAD — MIT; SpeechBrain — Apache 2.0;\n**NLLB-200 — CC-BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial use only)**.\n\n## Test results\n\nAll numbers come from runs on the target laptop; [TESTS.md](TESTS.md) has every run, the method and the raw values.\n\n### Armenian transcription and English translation\nThree sets of my own recordings with known correct text and reference translations (`eval/`): **read** (10 clearly\nread sentences), **natural** (6 colloquial sentences at normal call speed), **check** (5 sentences recorded later,\nused only to confirm the model change). Scored with `scripts/eval_asr.py` through the same path as the live program.\nCER/WER = character/word error rate after removing punctuation; English judged by hand as correct / gist / wrong.\n\n| Set | Model | CER | WER | English correct / gist / wrong | ASR max per phrase |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| read (10) | large-v3, beam 1 (previous) | 8.6 % | | 2 / 3 / 5 | 2.08 s |\n| read (10) | **turbo-armenian, beam 5** | **1.3 %** | 8.2 % | 9 / 1 / 0 (beam 1) | 1.89 s (all sets) |\n| natural (6) | large-v3, beam 1 | 27.2 % | | 0 / 3 / 3 | 2.63 s |\n| natural (6) | **turbo-armenian, beam 5** | **19.5 %** | 37.0 % | 2 / 2 / 2 (beam 1) | |\n| check (5) | large-v3, beam 1 | 11.6 % | | 0 / 2 / 3 | 2.87 s |\n| check (5) | **turbo-armenian, beam 5** | **5.6 %** | 17.5 % | 3 / 1 / 1 (beam 1, with punctuation cleanup) | |\n\n- Beam 5 vs beam 1 on turbo-armenian: better or equal on every set (all 21 sentences: CER 9.25 → 8.64 %). The gain is\n  smaller than the 1-point threshold I set before the test; it was adopted because nothing got worse and the latency\n  cost is ~0.1 s ([D-028](DECISIONS.md)). The English judgements were made with beam 1 and not repeated.\n- From the *correct* Armenian text NLLB translated 10/10 read sentences understandably: the remaining English errors\n  come mostly from transcription errors (e.g. «սուրջ» instead of «սուրճ» turned *coffee* into *seriously* with the\n  previous model).\n- Remaining typical errors: թ/տ and similar sounds («կատ» → \"goats\"), «Երեք» for «Երեկ», Russian words, words\n  split in two («Խոս ափող»).\n\n### Speaker identification\nThree 60–80 s interview recordings with known speaker changes (`scripts/speaker_test.py`):\n\n| Recording | Wrong labels at threshold 0.35 | Same speaker similarity | New speaker's first phrase |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| man + woman | 0 | 0.54–0.77 | 0.21 |\n| same gender | 0 (speaker returning after 20 s gets the same label) | 0.73–0.80 | 0.14 |\n| two women (laughing, overlap) | 0 | 0.51–0.88 | 0.16 |\n\nThresholds 0.35 and 0.4 gave 0 errors on all three recordings; 0.2 merged two speakers and 0.55 created extra ones.\nLive runs on two of the recordings gave the correct speakers. In a Zoom test with one helper, one short phrase\n(similarity 0.27) created an extra `Speaker 2`.\n\n### Latency (end of phrase → English line)\n\n| Run | Model | Within 5 s | Median | Max |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Live microphone, 2026-10-31 | turbo-armenian, beam 5 | 8/8 | 2.1 s | 2.7 s |\n| Zoom, 1 helper (Z1): `Me` / call side | turbo-armenian, beam 1 | 9/9 / 5/5 | 2.5 / 3.0 s | 4.4 / 4.0 s |\n| Zoom, 1 helper, both talking (Z2): `Me` / call side | turbo-armenian, beam 1 | 14/14 / 8/8 | 2.2 / 2.9 s | 3.1 / 5.0 s |\n| Interview played as call side + my speech | large-v3, beam 1 | 18/20 | 3.0–4.1 s | 5.9 s |\n| Overlapping speech + echo (before later fixes) | large-v3, beam 1 | 64–70 % | 4.1–4.8 s | 8.7 s |\n\nThe Zoom runs used beam 1, before beam 5 became the default; beam 5 adds ~0.1 s ASR time on the test sets.\n\n### Other checks\n- Both sources captured at the same time with 0 lost audio blocks (PortAudio problem flags 0 in all runs).\n- No phrase lost on Ctrl+C: detected = printed in every run (a shutdown bug that lost phrases was found and fixed).\n- **Offline**: full program with Wi-Fi off — all models load, no network access ([D-024](DECISIONS.md)).\n\n## Known limitations\n\n- **Armenian accuracy on natural speech.** CER is ~20 % on fast colloquial speech (1.3 % on clear reading). One\n  wrong letter can change the English meaning, and a wrongly added `՞` turns a statement into a question.\n- **Echo.** If call audio reaches the microphone, it is transcribed again as `Me` (echo handling is out of scope in\n  the brief). This happened in Zoom with a headset whose microphone is on the earphone cable: about 6 of 14 `Me`\n  blocks repeated the helper's words. Earphones without a microphone should avoid it but were not measured.\n- **Repetition filter.** It catches most Whisper loops but not all: a loop with 50 % different words was printed\n  and translated (the filter needs < 40 %). A real phrase that repeats the same words many times could be discarded.\n- **Mixed languages.** Russian and English words inside Armenian (out of scope in the brief) are written in Armenian\n  letters; translation recovers some (\"meeting\", \"Okay\") but not others.\n- **Latency under overlapping speech.** One GPU transcribes one phrase at a time. When both sides talk at once,\n  phrases wait; the 5 s target is not guaranteed. The first phrase after start-up is also slower.\n- **Phrase cutting.** Phrases are cut at 5 s to keep latency down; long sentences are split, which makes some\n  translations choppy. If the speaker changes inside a phrase, the whole phrase gets one label.\n- **Speaker identification** was tested on short recordings and Zoom calls with one other person; not on long\n  calls. Very short phrases can create an extra speaker or keep the closest known one.\n- **Platform.** Windows only (WASAPI loopback), an NVIDIA GPU is required; tested on one laptop.\n- **NLLB licence** is non-commercial.\n\n## What I would improve with more time\n\n1. **Echo:** drop a `Me` phrase that overlaps in time with a call-side phrase and has nearly the same text, or use\n   proper echo cancellation.\n2. **Accuracy:** a larger, more varied evaluation set (more speakers, real call audio); fine-tuning or evaluating\n   further Armenian models on it; a stricter but tested repetition filter.\n3. **Throughput under overlap:** transcribe several waiting phrases in one GPU batch, or use a faster GPU.\n4. **Smarter phrase cutting:** cut at short pauses near the 5 s limit; detect speaker changes inside a phrase.\n5. **Robustness and usability:** longer sessions with more people; tune the speaker threshold on call audio; pick\n   devices by name; handle headphones being plugged in during a session.\n\n## Repository layout\n\n```\nhylive/                 the program (python -m hylive)\nscripts/                tools used to build and test it:\n  gpu_smoke_test.py       GPU check            list_devices.py, record_test.py   devices / recordings\n  download_models.py      one-time setup       convert_test.py, vad_test.py       resampling / VAD checks\n  asr_test.py, mt_test.py ASR / MT checks      record_eval.py, eval_asr.py        evaluation sets + CER/WER/chrF\n  play_eval.py            play clips as call   speaker_test.py                    speaker ID thresholds\neval/                   evaluation sentences and reference translations (audio is not committed)\nPLAN.md                 original plan         DECISIONS.md   every decision with reasons and numbers\nTESTS.md                all test results      TIMELOG.md     time spent (20 h limit)\nHANDOVER.md             state / next steps between work sessions\nCLAUDE.md               project rules given to the AI assistant\nchats/                  complete, unedited AI chat transcripts (required by the brief)\nrequirements.txt        pinned package versions\n```\n\nNot committed (`.gitignore`): model weights (`models/`), audio recordings (`recordings/`, `eval/audio/`), the\nvirtual environment, secrets.\n\n## How this was built\n\nI worked with Claude Cowork as the only AI assistant, step by step: plan first, a thin end-to-end version early,\nthen improving the weakest part, deciding by measurements with rules set before each test. Every decision and test is\nwritten down in `DECISIONS.md` and `TESTS.md`; the complete conversations are in `chats/`.\nEOF\ngrep -n \"large-v3\" README.md | cut -c1-140; echo; git diff --stat"

## Results of the final 3-person Zoom test (1 min 40 s)

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| **Latency** | **33/33 within 5 s.** `Me`: median 2.6 s, max 4.1 s. Call side: median 2.7 s, max 3.3 s. Queue never above 2. |
| **Reliability** | 0 PortAudio flags, detected = printed on both sides, 1 loop correctly discarded. |
| **Speakers** | **2 speakers for 2 friends, no extra label.** Speaker 1 came back at 01:01 after Speaker 2 had spoken and got the same label (similarity 0.81). Each speaker's later phrases scored 0.50–0.86. |
| **Echo** | **13 of 22 `Me` blocks are your friends' voices** picked up by your mic (00:20–01:26, same timestamps as the call side). Only 9 `Me` blocks were really you. |
| **Overlap** | I can't see any overlapping speech in the output; it looks like it didn't happen. |

**Armenian recognition, call side (from the screen):** mostly good on long, fast sentences. The errors are similar-sounding words, e.g. «արդյող» for «արդյոք», «Այժմիայն» for «ոչ միայն», «անրաբեռնված» for «ծանրաբեռնված».

**English translation, call side (my judgement, 11 blocks):** about 6 correct, 2 gist, 3 wrong.
- Correct examples: "My week has been pretty busy, so I've got a lot to do every day.", "I had a lot of free time at the beginning of the week."
- The wrong ones are mostly **sentences cut by the 5-second limit**. «…ընտանիքի հետ ժամանակ անցկացնել» was split, and its second part became "That's when it's done."

**Your speech (9 real `Me` blocks):** 5 correct, 2 gist, 2 wrong (short fragments after a cut). Two more things:
- One translation dropped half the sentence (01:29: "I had a similar situation.").
- 00:02 lost its question mark, so the question became a statement.

## The one critical issue: echo

Echo is the only problem that would visibly hurt the interview demo. I recommend **not changing code** for it:
- An echo filter would have to hold back `Me` lines until the matching call-side line is transcribed. That adds latency (in this run some echoes printed *before* the call-side line).
- It would also go into the final submission untested live.

Instead: document it honestly (already a README limitation), and for the interview use **earphones without a mic**, or a separate headset mic held away from the earbuds.
